$comment: Dependabot alert dismissals (issue #1520).
A DISMISSAL IS NOT AN ACCEPTANCE. `dependency-alert-policy.json` records risk this repository
has decided to tolerate for a bounded time. This file records alerts that describe code the
repository does not contain, which is a different and stronger claim — so it is made where the
next reader will actually see it, on the alert itself, and not as a line in the tolerated list.
THE PLAN IS DATA BECAUSE THE REASONING IS THE POINT. Twelve alerts need the same paragraph
recorded against them; pasting it twelve times by hand records twelve slightly different
paragraphs, and records nothing at all about the criteria that picked those twelve. Declaring
the match here means the selection is reviewed in a pull request before it is ever executed.
WHY THE CODE IS UNREACHABLE, STATED CORRECTLY. An earlier draft of this said nitro-contracts is
"reachable only from automation/**". That is FALSE and was caught before any alert carried it:
16 files in @chainlink/contracts@1.5.0 import nitro, and 11 of them are outside automation/ --
including `shared/util/ChainSpecificUtil.sol` and three under `functions/`, i.e. the two
directories this repo DOES import from. A future reader grepping for nitro under shared/ would
have found a hit and concluded the dismissal was wrong.
The real argument is stronger and does not depend on where nitro is imported from: solc reads a
CLOSURE, not a directory. The four chainlink paths contracts/ imports close over exactly 11
files, and that closure contains NO non-relative imports at all -- it cannot reach node_modules,
so it reaches neither OpenZeppelin nor nitro. Re-derive it against the installed package with
`scripts/security/chainlink-closure.js`; the count is asserted by the fixtures.
SELECTION IS BY PROOF, NEVER BY ALERT NUMBER. `compiledVersion` is the version this repository
actually compiles against, and an alert is only eligible when the advisory's vulnerable range
EXCLUDES it. An unparseable range counts as including it. That is what makes the plan safe to
re-run: bump the pin into a vulnerable range and the alerts stop matching rather than being
dismissed anyway, and X-02 fails the moment `compiledVersion` and package.json disagree.
`expectedCount` is the other half of that. The script refuses to apply when the live selection
is a different size than what was reviewed — a set that grew is a set nobody looked at.

dismissals.comment: Unreachable: solc never reads it. The import closure of the 4 chainlink paths contracts/ uses is 11 files with NO external imports at all - no OpenZeppelin, no nitro, nothing from node_modules. Compiled OZ is 5.4.0, outside every range. #1520
